Definition: from G2725; a complaint ("category"), i.e. criminal charge:--accusation (X -ed).
BiblicalUsage: The accusation is the complaint brought against a man, and Pilate asked what accusation the Jews brought against Jesus, and Paul says no accusation against an elder is to be received without two or three witnesses, and an elder must be blameless with faithful children and no accusation of riot. The word guards the accused as much as it charges him, because a charge without witnesses is no charge at all.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God guards His servants with the witness rule, because a single voice should never ruin a man. I hold that the accusation against Jesus was the one charge that could not stand, and the court that heard it condemned an innocent man anyway.
